analysis: Population bridge and stimulus-conditioned dependence sensitivity
status: Retrospective sensitivity analysis; choices recorded before executing this new analysis, not prospectively registered with the original experiment
count_analysis: Recompute the original all-cell one-second pooled count law. Decompose average neuronal marginal KL to its common Gibbs reference into pooled KL plus cell-identity information (Jensen-Shannon divergence). Exact empirical-distribution identities, not unbiased entropy estimates.
subsets: For each seed and group size m, sample 32 unique sorted neuron subsets from all 75 cells using seed+110900+m. Identical subsets across learning stages and budgets. Groups need not be disjoint and are averaged within a trained seed; they are not inferential replicates.
shuffle: At each fixed input-template and relative count-window index, independently permute repeat indices for each neuron. Each shuffle exactly preserves the conditional and unconditional marginal occupancy distributions, all-cell pooled occupancy law, expected activity and stimulus/time tuning; it changes cross-neuron trial coordination. Use identical permutation streams across paired stages and budgets.
metric: Total correlation TC=sum_i H2(Y_i)-H2(Y_group), in bits/group-window. Report observed TC, mean stimulus-conditioned shuffled TC and their signed difference. The signed excess is not calibrated population MI, noise entropy, or an unbiased total-correlation estimator; the shuffled law retains signal-induced dependence.
statistics: Average groups and shuffles within each trained seed. Eight training seeds define paired endpoint inference. Exact two-sided sign-flip tests of the change in signed shuffle excess, Holm adjusted across three budgets only for the primary 20-ms four-cell diagnostic. All other settings are descriptive sensitivities. No inference based on treating windows, groups or shuffles as independent trainings.
scope: No new training, no 75-dimensional joint entropy estimate, no whole-population optimality conclusion, no equivalence between count and occupancy response supports. Preserve original primary G and reconstruction results and every old figure byte-for-byte.
